corpusSummary: The corpus assembles a diverse set of 2026 social-science studies on large language models, highlighting themes of LLM behavior and bias, methodological use of LLMs in research and governance, AI in education and health, and the social dynamics of AI adoption and polarization. Across fields, researchers probe trust, fairness, evaluation, and ethical integration, while testing AI’s limits and opportunities.

themes.name: Mimicry, bias, and trust in LLMs
themes.description: A body of work examines how LLMs mirror or diverge from human cognition and social behavior, revealing attention to anthropomorphism, bias, and the need for reliability, fairness, and mitigation strategies.

themes.name: LLMs as social-science tools and governance frameworks
themes.description: Researchers explore using LLMs for data extraction, coding, simulation, and policy analysis while emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical governance to guide responsible use.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Studies address AI tutoring, classroom integration, and learner trust, investigating AI-based learning tools and their effects on engagement, literacy, and pedagogy across diverse populations.

themes.name: AI in health communication, misinformation, and equity
themes.description: A cluster of work analyzes AI-driven misinformation, health information quality, patient education, and equity considerations in deploying digital health AI.

themes.name: Social dynamics, polarization, and AI adoption
themes.description: Research into AI-enabled social systems examines how LLM agents, adoption patterns, and crisis-response tools shape networks, polarization, and collective creativity, including interventions for diversity and responsible use.

emergingKeywords: AI in education and teacher adoption
